fields.sample_size: 36 interviews with actors implementing sanitation innovations, Ministry, Nairobi County and Water Board officials, NGO, CBO and international agency representatives; three initiatives (Sanergy: 1,134 container-based toilets, 53,436 daily users; Umande Trust: 42 biocentres, 5,000 daily users; Peepoople: biodegradable bags to 100 schools, 18,000 children a day)
fields.effect_estimate: Applies a Technological Innovation System (TIS) analysis to sanitation value chains in Nairobi informal settlements and identifies system failures -- capability, coordination and institutional barriers (including regulation and fee/permit issues for emptying and disposal) -- proposing alternative governance modes to overcome them. Qualitative; usage figures are programme-reported, not evaluated.
fields.study_design: qualitative multiple-case study (36 interviews; three initiatives; TIS framework)
fields.section: Full text: Methods (36 interviews, appendix of codes); Results (three sanitation value-chain initiatives, system failures); Discussion (governance modes)
fields.exact_location: Methods (36 interviews, appendix of codes); Results (three sanitation value-chain initiatives, system failures); Discussion (governance modes)

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a Technological Innovation System analysis of three on-site sanitation value-chain initiatives in Nairobi informal settlements (36 interviews), read in full text 2026-10-04. Capability, coordination and institutional barriers are the system failures; alternative governance modes proposed. Programme-reported reach figures.
pdf_note: Environmental Innovation and Societal Transitions (2019) accepted manuscript, about 115,000 characters read
notes: Abstract-level extraction accurate; adds n = 36 and initiative sizes (programme-reported).
